items.summary: Mac Native 0.3.1 Beta has an official Modrinth release. Here is what the public record confirms and what it does not.
items.body:
## The publication
Mac Native 0.3.1 is listed as a beta release on the official Modrinth project. Its published compatibility is Minecraft: Java Edition 1.21.11, Fabric and client-side use. The project description addresses Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. These are compatibility statements, not a guarantee of a particular frame rate or battery life.

## What changed
The release notes mention network changes involving e4all and VMP, configuration for AsyncParticles and ModernFix, and updates to default options. For an exact list of files and dependencies, follow the release Content tab. The Labs does not reproduce unverified benchmark numbers as an independent test.

## Install from the publisher
Use the official release link on the [Mac Native page](/modpacks/mac-native), check its loader and game version, and keep a backup of your worlds. If the project publishes a newer version, its Modrinth release page remains the source of truth. The [Mac Native guide](/guides/complete-mac-native) explains a careful installation workflow.

items.summary: A careful route from the official release page to a separate instance on macOS.
items.body:
## Begin with compatibility
Mac Native is published for Minecraft Java 1.21.11 with Fabric in its current verified release. Before downloading, compare those fields with the pack you intend to play. macOS support covers Apple Silicon and Intel in the project description, but hardware results vary.

## Keep a separate instance
Install the pack from the official Modrinth project into a new launcher instance. This keeps another pack or vanilla world from being silently changed. Sign in with an account that owns Minecraft: Java Edition. A different launcher can import compatible packs, but its own documentation should control the exact steps.

## Make changes reversible
Launch once with the published defaults. Back up worlds before updates or adding optional mods. If it crashes, capture the launcher log and compare version, loader and recent changes. Use the [complete guide](/guides/complete-mac-native) and [support](/support) instead of relying on a universal RAM or shader setting.

items.summary: CraftToons remains an in-development concept, with no public release or download to announce.
items.body:
## A different experience
The public CraftToons page is deliberately a teaser. It names the project and communicates that development is under way. It does not publish a build, version, date, feature list or download link. A concept can be interesting without pretending to be available.

## How to follow it
The [CraftToons page](/modpacks/crafttoons) is the stable destination for approved information. When a release is actually published, the project can receive compatibility and distribution facts through Content V2. Until then, Mac Native is the publicly usable beta product.

## Editorial boundary
Screenshots or descriptions from early experiments should not be treated as promised features. We will separate working concepts from releases in the same way that the Labs separates internal status from public version numbers.

items.summary: A look at the Git-first workflow behind projects, guides and news.
items.body:
## A versioned public source
Projects, releases, launchers, articles, guides, FAQ and website settings have validated V2 records in the repository. Published JSON is bundled with the site so a public route cannot accidentally read a private draft. A schema checks fields before publication.

## Draft, preview, publish
The owner workspace uses authentication, a private draft, preview and a server-side publishing function. The function checks the expected Git revision before committing to the Preview branch, preventing a quiet overwrite of newer work. A Git commit still needs a Vercel Preview build before the changed page is ready.

## Why it matters to readers
A stable URL can keep its history while an article is reviewed and improved. Editorial translations can be incomplete; the original text remains available rather than automatically fabricating translations. See the [News archive](/news) and [Guides](/guides) for currently published entries.

items.summary: Why the official download destination matters more than a rating badge.
items.body:
## Know the publisher
Minecraft launchers can manage separate instances, Java versions and modpacks, but a third-party launcher is not a substitute for a legitimate game account. Follow the developer’s own website or release page; a shortened historical link is not proof of provenance.

## Compare a concrete workflow
Prism supports independent instances and pack sources including Modrinth and CurseForge. Modrinth App focuses on content from its own platform. ATLauncher and others have their own installation paths. These are different workflows, not a universal ranking. Check the OS, loader and source of the pack you need.

## Read further
The [launcher catalog](/launchers) keeps source links and verification dates where reviewed. Our [Prism guide](/guides/prism-launcher-setup) walks through one instance. Always confirm that documentation matches the specific release you download.

items.summary: The FAQ connects common questions to projects, launchers and support.
items.body:
## Start with the project
The [FAQ](/faq) covers accounts, project status, compatibility, downloads and support. It should answer what is known and send version-specific questions to the published project or release. Mac Native is a beta; CraftToons is in development without a public release.

## Find the right document
A guide can describe a sequence in more detail than a short FAQ answer. A launcher page tells you where the developer publishes downloads, while a project page links to the pack’s official source. Keep game versions and loaders in view when moving between them.

## Ask with context
If you still need help, include the project, release, operating system, launcher and error log where safe. Never send passwords, access tokens or private account information. The [support page](/support) provides the current contact routes.

items.summary: Downloads and followers are live public counters, not independent quality reviews or benchmarks.
items.body:
## Live data and editorial facts
The Labs reads download and follower counts from the official public Modrinth project API. The response is cached for a short interval and the numbers disappear if the API is unavailable; a network error never becomes a false zero. A release version and changelog are editorially validated separately.

## Do not overread counts
A download is an event counted by the platform. It does not prove performance, active users or satisfaction. Followers measure an action on Modrinth, not a review score. Comparisons require a defined method, device and repeatable conditions.

## Check the source
Open the [Mac Native publication](https://modrinth.com/modpack/mac-native) for live platform information. On the [project page](/modpacks/mac-native), compatibility and release facts stay usable even when the metrics endpoint fails.

items.summary: Guides connect a question to a safe installation or troubleshooting sequence.
items.body:
## Practical paths
The first [Guides](/guides) cover Mac Native installation, Prism setup, the distinction between AstralRinth and Modrinth App, and the basic ideas behind launchers and modpacks. Each should provide a starting point, a sequence, and a path when something goes wrong.

## Version-aware advice
A guide must not pretend to detect hardware or prescribe a single memory setting for every machine. Before following a step, compare the date of the guide with the release and consult the publisher’s current compatibility. Back up worlds before changing instances.

## Keep learning
Use the linked primary sources to verify changing technical details. If a step does not match what you see, ask through [support](/support) with the application version and a redacted error log. The library can be updated through the owner CMS without replacing the page architecture.
